title: Factorization with a geometrically integral generic curve
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper dominant morphism of integral excellent Noetherian schemes. Suppose that its generic fibre is geometrically integral of dimension $d\geq2$. There are integral excellent Noetherian schemes $X',Y$ and a factorization $f\pi=h g$, with $\pi:X'\to X$ a proper birational modification, and $g:X'\to Y$ and $h:Y\to S$ proper dominant morphisms. The generic fibres of $g$ and $h$ are geometrically integral, of dimensions $1$ and $d-1$, respectively. If $S$ and $X$ have finite dimension, so do $Y$ and $X'$. Here a proper birational modification is a proper morphism that is an isomorphism over a dense open of its integral target.

Properness, integrality, excellence, Noetherianness, fibres, geometric integrality, dimension and generic points use [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [pqf-def-locnoeth], [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], [def-pc-scheme-fibre], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and [def-sc-generic-point].

source.place: Lemma 5.2 and its proof, printed pp. 612--613, with trivial group; forget projectivity. The dimensions are the stated relative curve dimension and the complementary transcendence degree; finiteness of total dimensions follows from Stacks Tag 02JX (morphisms-lemma-alteration-dimension). Local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online.

proof.text: Put $K=k(S)$ and $M=k(X)$. The generic fibre $X_\eta$ is a proper integral $K$-variety: on an affine chart over $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq S$ its rings are localizations by $B\setminus\{0\}$; they are domains and their common generic point has residue field $M$. Properness follows by base change. A nonempty affine chart has fraction field $M$ and a finite list of algebra generators, so $M/K$ is finitely generated. The dimension--transcendence-degree theorem gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_K M=d$. Moreover $\operatorname{Spec}M$ is geometrically integral over $K$: take a nonempty affine open $U\subseteq X_\eta$, which is geometrically integral by the definition, and apply the affine function-field transfer lemma to $U$ and $\operatorname{Spec}M$, using their identical fraction fields. Thus $M\otimes_KE$ is a domain for every field extension $E/K$.

source.place: Tags 054Q and 0A21 (item 0B1C); Tag 0559, first proof, passage to the function field; morphisms Tag 01RV

proof.text: Choose a separating transcendence basis $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $M/K$. In characteristic zero the perfect-field separating-basis lemma applies. In characteristic $p>0$, the reducedness of every $M\otimes_KE$ from step 1 implies separability by the geometrically-reduced-extension lemma; apply its definition to the finitely generated subextension $M$ itself. The cardinality of the basis is $d$ by the definition of transcendence degree. Put $F=K(t_1,\ldots,t_{d-1})$. Then $t_d$ is a separating transcendence basis of $M/F$, since $M/K(t_1,\ldots,t_d)$ is separable algebraic. In particular $M/F$ is separably generated and has transcendence degree one. Tensoring it with any extension field of $F$ is reduced by the separably-generated tensor theorem.

source.place: Tags 030O, 030W and 030U; de Jong Lemma 5.2, proof, p. 613, choice of d−1 functions

proof.text: Let $P=\mathbf P^{d-1}_S$. Its standard charts over an affine domain $B$ in $S$ are polynomial rings in $d-1$ variables over $B$. The charts are integral, have nonempty pairwise overlaps, and have the same generic point, so $P$ is integral, with function field $F$, and is proper dominant over $S$. Choose a nonempty affine $V\subseteq X$ mapping into an affine open of $S$. Express the finitely many $t_i$, $i<d$, as fractions in $\mathcal O_X(V)$, and invert the product of their nonzero denominators. On the resulting dense affine open $U\subseteq X$ they define the map $[1:t_1:\cdots:t_{d-1}]$ into the first chart of $P$. This is an $S$-morphism $r_0:U\to P$. Algebraic independence makes the map from the coordinate domain of that chart injective, hence $r_0$ maps the generic point to the generic point and is dominant.

source.place: Tag 01NG, lemma-standard-covering-projective-space; morphisms Tag 01RV; de Jong Lemma 5.2, rational map

proof.text: Form the scheme-theoretic image $Z$ of $(1,r_0):U\to X\times_SP$, and write $a:Z\to X$ and $r_Z:Z\to P$ for the projections. The map is quasi-compact: $U$ is Noetherian, so all its open subsets are quasi-compact. The image lemmas give that $|Z|$ is the closure of the irreducible nonempty graph, hence irreducible and nonempty; they also give $a^{-1}(U)\simeq U$. For an affine open $W$ of the product meeting $Z$, its inverse image in $U$ is nonempty by density. Sections there inject into $M$. The defining ideal on $W$ is the kernel of the map to these sections, hence is prime. Thus every affine chart of $Z$ has a domain as coordinate ring, so $Z$ is reduced and integral. The dense open $a^{-1}(U)$ identifies its function field with $M$.

source.place: Tags 01R8 and 01R7, scheme-theoretic image and its affine kernels; partial-section image over U

proof.text: The two projections of $X\times_SP$ are proper by base change, and the inclusion of $Z$ is closed. Thus $a$ and $r_Z$ are proper. Their images contain respectively $U$ and $r_0(U)$, so both are dominant. Consequently $Z\to S$ is proper. The schemes $P$ and $Z$ are Noetherian by finite type over the Noetherian base. They are excellent as well: over an affine excellent chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq S$, the locally finite type affine-pairs lemma makes the coordinate rings of source affine charts finite type over $B$. Excellence ascends to these rings, and the affine-cover excellence lemma gives excellence on every affine open.

source.place: Tags 01W3, 01W4, 01W8 and 01T1; more-algebra Tag 07QU; morphisms Tag 0HAB

proof.text:
Normalize $Z$ in $M=k(Z)$, obtaining $
u:X\prime	o Z$. The residue-field normalization lemma gives an integral normal $X\prime$ with function field $M$. This map is finite: each excellent affine domain $B\subset M$ is quasi-excellent, hence Nagata, hence N-2 by taking its zero prime; its integral closure $\overline B\subset M$ is a finite $B$-module. The localization theorem identifies these finite affine normalization rings on overlaps. This also shows directly that $
u$ is an isomorphism over a dense open: take a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Z$ and finite module generators of $\overline B$, write them as fractions in $B$, and invert the product $b
e0$ of their denominators. Then $\overline B[1/b]=B[1/b]$. Choose the affine inside $a^{-1}(U)$; the composite $\pi=a
u$ is an isomorphism over the corresponding dense open of $X$.

source.place: Tags 035H, 035I and 035L; more-algebra Tag 07QV (quasi-excellent implies Nagata); algebra Tag 0307

proof.text: The finite map $\nu$ is proper, so $\pi$ and $X\prime\to S$ are proper. The finite-type arguments of step 5 show that $X\prime$ is excellent and Noetherian. Put $r=r_Z\nu:X\prime\to P$. It is proper by composition and dominant because it induces the inclusion $F\subset M$. Let $T=X\prime\times_P\operatorname{Spec}F$. This is a proper integral $F$-variety with function field $M$. It is normal: over an affine chart of $P$, formation of this generic fibre inverts the nonzero elements of its coordinate domain. At a point of $T$ all those elements are already units in the local ring of $X\prime$, so the local rings of $T$ are the same integrally closed domains. No smoothness of $T$ is asserted.

source.place: Tags 01WM, 01W3 and 01W4; de Jong Lemma 5.2, normal modification before Stein factorization

proof.text: Take $\mathcal B=r_*\mathcal O_{X\prime}$ and $q:Y=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_P(\mathcal B)\to P$. Proper coherent pushforward makes $\mathcal B$ a coherent, hence quasi-coherent, finite $\mathcal O_P$-algebra; here $\mathcal O_{X\prime}$ is coherent since $X\prime$ is Noetherian (on a Noetherian affine, kernels between finite free modules are finite). Relative spectrum gives $q^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(r^{-1}V,\mathcal O)$ for each affine $V\subseteq P$, and $q$ is finite by the finite-morphism criterion. The identity on this section algebra defines the local evaluation map $r^{-1}V\to q^{-1}V$. These maps agree on overlaps: restriction of the algebra and of its relative spectrum commutes with open restriction, and maps to an affine are determined by their maps on sections. They therefore glue to $g:X\prime\to Y$ with $r=qg$.

source.place: Tag 03H0, theorem-stein-factorization-Noetherian, relative-spectrum construction; coherent Tag 02O5; morphisms Tag 01SA

proof.text: The map $g$ is dominant. Indeed, on $q^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B_V$, sections $B_V=\Gamma(r^{-1}V,\mathcal O)$ inject into $M$. A nonempty principal open $D(b)$ has $b\ne0$; this section cannot vanish at every point of the reduced scheme $r^{-1}V$, so $g^{-1}D(b)$ is nonempty. These principal opens form a basis, and the affine opens $q^{-1}V$ cover $Y$. Therefore $Y$ is irreducible, since it contains the dense image of the irreducible $X\prime$. Its rings $B_V$ are domains, so $Y$ is reduced and integral. The finite $q$ is proper, hence $h:Y\to P\to S$ is proper; $q$ is dominant because $qg=r$ is dominant, and thus so is $h$. Since $h$ is separated and $hg=f\pi$ is proper, the proper-over-separated lemma makes $g$ proper. Finite type over $P$ and then $S$ also makes $Y$ Noetherian and excellent by exactly the affine-cover argument of step 5.

source.place: Tag 03H0, theorem-stein-factorization-Noetherian; morphisms Tag 01W6 and Tag 0HAB

proof.text: Put $L=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The proper-variety global-sections theorem says that $L/F$ is a finite field extension. Restrict to a nonempty affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq P$. Flat base change of global sections along $B\to F$ identifies $\Gamma(r^{-1}V,\mathcal O)\otimes_BF$ with $L$. This is a ring isomorphism: on pure tensors it sends $s\otimes c$ to $c$ times the restricted section $s$, so preserves products and the unit. Consequently $Y\times_P\operatorname{Spec}F=\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $k(Y)=L$; the generic fibre of $g$ is precisely $T$ regarded as an $L$-variety. Furthermore $L$ is algebraically closed in $M$. If $z\in M$ is algebraic over $L$, its monic polynomial over $L$ has coefficients regular on all of $T$. Thus $z$ is integral over each local ring of $T$, and normality puts it in each such ring. Local representatives agree in the common field $M$, so glue to a global section: $z\in L$. Finally $L/F$ is separable algebraic: every element $a\in L$ belongs to the finitely generated algebraic subextension $F(a)/F$ of the separable extension $M/F$, so the definition of separability gives an empty separating transcendence basis and hence separability of $a$.

source.place: Proper-variety constants; more-morphisms Tag 03H0 and coherent Tag 02KH; de Jong Lemma 5.2, constants of the normal generic fibre

proof.text: By step 2 the $F$-algebra $M$ is geometrically reduced, and by step 10 $L/F$ is separable algebraic. Apply the scalar-restriction lemma to this $L$-algebra $M$: for every extension $E/L$, $M\otimes_LE$ is reduced. The generic-stalk reducedness criterion, applied to the integral $L$-variety $T$ with its sole generic stalk $M$, therefore proves that $T$ is geometrically reduced over $L$. The finite-separable-closure lemma applied to $M/L$ makes it geometrically irreducible after taking the separable algebraic closure of $L$ in $M$. That closure is $L$ itself by step 10. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}M$ is geometrically irreducible over $L$, and the generic-point criterion makes $T$ geometrically irreducible. Combining reducedness and irreducibility after every field extension proves that the generic fibre of $g$ is geometrically integral.

source.place: Tags 04KS, 054Q and algebra Tag 037Q; algebra Tag 0C2Y; de Jong Lemma 5.2, geometric integrality of the first generic fibre

proof.text: For every extension field $E/K$, the inclusion $L\subset M$ gives an injection $L\otimes_KE\hookrightarrow M\otimes_KE$: $E$ is flat over $K$ and flatness preserves injections. The latter ring is a domain by step 1, so the former is a domain as well; it is nonzero because it contains the unit of that domain. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is geometrically integral over $K$. The generic fibre $Y_\eta$ of $h$ is integral with function field $L$, by localization on its affine charts. The generic-point irreducibility criterion makes $Y_\eta$ geometrically irreducible. The generic-stalk reducedness criterion applied to these tensor products makes it geometrically reduced. It is therefore geometrically integral. Since $L/F$ is finite algebraic and $\operatorname{trdeg}_KF=d-1$, the tower formula gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_KL=d-1$ and $\operatorname{trdeg}_LM=1$. Apply the dimension--transcendence-degree theorem to the integral proper varieties $Y_\eta/K$ and $T/L$ to obtain dimensions $d-1$ and $1$.

source.place: Tags 054Q, 04KS and 0B1C; fields Tag 030H; de Jong Lemma 5.2, second generic fibre

proof.text: The equality $hg=f\pi$ follows from $qg=r=r_Z\nu$ and the two projections of the graph over $S$. We have proved all the required integrality, properness, dominance and dimension assertions, and step 6 gives the dense-open isomorphism required of $\pi$. For the last clause, apply the closed-dominant dimension theorem to the proper birational map $\pi$: it gives $\dim X\prime=\dim X$, because its function-field extension is the identity. Apply the same theorem to $h$ to get $\dim Y=\dim S+(d-1)$. Hence $X\prime$ and $Y$ have finite dimension whenever $X$ and $S$ do.
